## JNJ — Quantitative Fundamental-Attractiveness Report
**Decision date: 2026-05-22**

---

### 1. Revenue, Earnings & Margin Trajectory

Revenue has grown sequentially over the four available quarters: Q1 $21.89B → Q2 $23.74B → Q3 $23.99B → Q4 $24.06B. However, growth is decelerating sharply — Q1→Q2 +8.5%, Q2→Q3 +1.1%, Q3→Q4 +0.3%. TTM revenue stands at $93.69B. No prior-year YoY comparison is available in this window.

EPS tells a distorted story. Q1 (period_end 2025-03-30) reported EPS of $4.54 and operating income of $13.63B — both roughly double the subsequent three quarters ($2.12–$2.29 EPS; $5.99B–$7.49B operating income). This is almost certainly a one-time gain (likely an asset divestiture or spin-off event). The TTM net income of $26.92B is therefore overstated relative to the underlying run-rate.

**Normalized earnings power:** Excluding Q1's anomalous $11.00B net income and substituting the Q2–Q4 average of ~$5.31B/quarter, the sustainable quarterly net income is approximately $5.3B, implying a normalized annual run-rate of ~$21.2B or ~$8.72 EPS diluted (vs. the TTM-reported $26.92B). At a Q4 EPS of $2.14, the current run-rate EPS is closer to $8.56 annualized.

Gross margin compressed in Q4 to 66.3% (15.96B / 24.06B) from 69.6% in Q3, as cost of revenue rose to $8.11B from $7.30B. Operating margin fell to 24.9% in Q4 (vs. 31.2% in Q3). Net margin held at 21.8% — essentially flat with Q3 (21.5%) because Q3's operating margin advantage was offset by tax or below-the-line items.

### 2. Earnings Quality & Cash Generation

The Q1 outlier degrades reported earnings quality for the trailing period. Once Q1 rolls out of the TTM window, reported earnings will reset lower.

Cash generation is a concern. Operating cash flow was only $2.51B in Q4 — a 72.6% QoQ decline from Q3's $9.17B. TTM operating cash flow totals $19.73B. Against a normalized net income of ~$21B, cash conversion appears below 1.0x, and the Q4 quarter in particular was weak. Free cash flow is unavailable in this dataset.

The balance sheet remains sound: total equity of $81.19B, cash of $22.05B (up from $18.56B in Q3), total liabilities of $119.71B, implying a debt-to-equity of ~1.47x — moderate for a healthcare major. Total assets grew to $200.89B from $192.82B in Q3, partly reflecting the cash build and likely asset revaluation.

### 3. Valuation Versus Own History

This is where the case becomes most compelling — in the wrong direction. The current PE of 26.93x sits at the **absolute ceiling** of the 365-day window (range: 16.6–26.9x). One year ago (2025-05-22) the PE was 16.96x. The PE has expanded by 59% in twelve months.

Critically, this re-rating occurred while **normalized margins and earnings are compressing, not expanding.** Net margin fell from 0.273 (Oct 2025) to 0.218 (latest). ROE dropped from 0.317 to 0.259. P/B has expanded from 4.74x to 6.98x — again near the ceiling of its 4.6–7.6 range. Earnings yield is a meager 3.7%.

If we normalize annual EPS to ~$8.56 (Q4 run-rate × 4), the "true" forward PE on sustainable earnings is even higher than the reported 26.9x — closer to **27.1x** at the $231.73 price. This is a premium multiple for a company exhibiting zero sequential revenue growth and declining operating margins.

### 4. Price Context

Price closed at $231.73 on 2026-05-21. The 52-week range is $149.04–$251.71, placing the stock 8% below the high and 56% above the low. The quarterly path shows a pullback of -4.4% from the Feb 20 close of $242.49, following a +21.2% run from Nov ($200.00) to Feb. The price has essentially re-rated to reflect peak multiples while the fundamental backdrop is flat-to-softening.

### 5. Macro & Sentiment Overlays

**Rates are the key macro headwind.** The 10-year Treasury yield stands at 4.57% — up 54 bps over 90 days. JNJ's earnings yield of 3.7% sits **below** the 10Y yield by 87 bps. This is the opposite of the historical defensive-valuation relationship; a stable healthcare compounder typically needs an earnings yield premium to the risk-free rate to justify its multiple. In a 4.5%+ rate regime, a 26.9x PE on decelerating earnings is particularly expensive.

Corporate credit spreads (Baa at 6.16%) are moderately elevated, though JNJ's AA-rated balance sheet insulates it from credit repricing. The VIX has fallen to 16.76 (down 20.2% over 90 days), suggesting the "fear bid" into defensives may be fading. Oil at $100.2/bbl is an input cost risk for the broader economy and pharmaceutical logistics.

News sentiment is mildly positive (mean 0.567 over 97 articles in 90 days) but offers no fundamental insight — mood is not earnings.

### 6. Strongest Quantitative Upside & Downside

**Upside:** If the Q1 2025 one-time item reflects a business simplification (e.g., Kenvue spin completion), the post-spin operating structure may support higher sustainable margins over time. The gross margin of 66–70% remains industry-leading. The balance sheet ($22B cash, moderate leverage) provides resilience.

**Downside:** (a) The PE is at a 12-month ceiling while normalized earnings are deteriorating — mean reversion in the multiple from 26.9x to the 1-year median (~19.5x) would imply ~28% downside in the absence of earnings growth. (b) Operating cash flow collapsed 72.6% QoQ in Q4 — if this is structural rather than timing, cash returns (dividends/buybacks) may come under pressure. (c) Rising Treasury yields structurally compress defensive multiples; each 50bps move in the 10Y could warrant 2–3 turns of PE compression. (d) The Q1 outlier will roll out of TTM in the next filing, mechanically inflating reported PE further if price holds.

### 7. Provisional Conclusion

JNJ is **quantitatively unattractive** on fundamental-attractiveness grounds. The company is priced at peak multiples (~27x PE, ~7x P/B) against a backdrop of flat sequential revenue growth (+0.3% QoQ), margin compression (operating margin 24.9% in Q4 vs 31.2% in Q3), weakening cash generation (OCF -72.6% QoQ), and earnings quality degraded by a prior-period one-time gain. The rising rate environment (10Y at 4.57%) makes the 3.7% earnings yield look particularly unappealing relative to risk-free alternatives. The price has already re-rated +59% in PE terms over twelve months; the fundamental path does not support further multiple expansion, and normalized earnings appear to be declining, not growing. The risk/reward skews to the downside — the mean-reversion case on the multiple alone, from 26.9x to the 12-month midpoint of ~19.5x, represents meaningful valuation headwind even before considering margin trajectory.

# Johnson & Johnson (JNJ) — Qualitative Assessment
**Decision Date: 2026-05-22**

---

## 1. Business / Franchise Read

Following the 2023 Kenvue spin-off, Johnson & Johnson is a focused, two-segment healthcare company: **Innovative Medicine** (~64% of FY2025 revenue, ~84% of pre-tax profit) and **MedTech** (~36% of revenue). FY2025 consolidated revenue was $94.2B with operating margins of 26.8% and free cash flow of $19.7B. The company carries a AAA credit rating and has increased its dividend for 64 consecutive years.

The franchise quality is high by structural measures. Morningstar assigns JNJ one of the widest economic moats in healthcare, supported by intellectual property in pharma and switching costs in MedTech, with ROIC estimated in the midteens approaching 20% versus a 7.2% cost of capital. The Innovative Medicine segment is anchored by 28 products generating over $1B in annual sales, with particular strength in oncology (Darzalex at $14.35B in FY2025, up 23%), immunology (Tremfya at $5.2B, up 40.5%), and a rapidly scaling CAR-T franchise (Carvykti). Approximately two-thirds of Innovative Medicine revenue comes from chronic-disease therapies, creating recurring demand streams.

MedTech provides diversification into procedure-based growth categories — electrophysiology, cardiovascular (bolstered by the Abiomed and Shockwave Medical acquisitions), surgery, orthopaedics, and vision — that are less dependent on patent cycles. The strategic rationale is clear: Innovative Medicine drives higher margins and cash flow, while MedTech adds exposure to device-installed-base pull-through and procedural volume growth, including emerging robotic surgery platforms.

Capital allocation is disciplined. The company invests heavily in R&D (~$15.9B in 2025 per Statista) and pursues selective strategic M&A (Abiomed ~2022, Shockwave Medical $13.1B in 2024, Intra-Cellular Therapies $14.5B). Management has articulated an ambition to become the #1 oncology company by 2030 with over $50B in oncology revenue. The structural growth algorithm is mid-single-digit top- and bottom-line growth, funded by portfolio renewal against mature-product headwinds.

## 2. Recent Developments (News + Updates)

**Earnings momentum continues.** Q1 2026 results (reported April 2026) showed revenue of ~$24.06B (+9.9% YoY) and adjusted EPS of $2.70, beating consensus. The Innovative Medicine segment grew revenue +11.2% operationally, driven by Darzalex, Carvykti, Erleada, Rybrevant/Lazcluze, Tremfya, and Spravato. MedTech grew +7.7%. Management guided FY2026 revenue to $100.3–$101.3B and adjusted EPS of $11.45–$11.65, bracketing consensus and signaling confidence.

**Pipeline clinical data.** On 2026-05-17, Nanobiotix presented Part 1 data from the CONVERGE Phase 2 trial of JNJ-1900 (NBTXR3), a nanoradioenhancer for stage 3 inoperable NSCLC, showing an 85.7% overall response rate and 57.1% complete response rate in 7 evaluable patients, compared to <5% complete response with current standard of care. This is early and small-sample data, but directionally positive for the lung cancer pipeline. (Note: the 2026-05-19 ImmunityBio ANKTIVA bladder cancer data article references competitive dynamics in the bladder cancer space but does not directly involve JNJ products.)

**Oncology pipeline depth.** Morningstar's updated fair value estimate of $190 reflects increased confidence in Inlexzo (bladder cancer, ~$3B peak sales) and Icotyde (immunology, ~$7B peak), alongside Tremfya expansion (~$14B peak). The structural web search confirms JNJ's ambition to reach $50B in oncology revenue by 2030, with oncology operational sales growing at 22.3% in Q2 2025.

**Dividend and defensive positioning.** Multiple recent articles (Motley Fool, 2026-05-17 and 2026-05-19) frame JNJ as a Dividend King and defensive holding suitable for market-downturn accumulation, reflecting its 64-year streak and AAA rating.

## 3. Material Risks and Offsets

**Stelara biosimilar erosion is the single largest near-term headwind.** Stelara revenue fell from ~$10B+ to $6.08B in FY2025 (-41.3%) as US biosimilars launched in January 2025. The structural web search and Trefis analysis frame this as the central investment debate: can accelerating growth from the new portfolio fully absorb this ~50% franchise decline? Q1 2026 results (+9.9% revenue growth) suggest the offset is working so far, but the drag will persist through 2026–2027.

**Talc litigation remains unquantified.** Though the Kenvue separation was designed to ring-fence talc exposure, structural sources confirm the legal and reputational overhang persists. This is a structural risk that cannot be precisely sized from available text.

**IRA and pricing pressure.** Government price negotiations under the Inflation Reduction Act threaten margins on selected blockbusters (Xarelto noted specifically). This is a multi-year structural risk to pricing power in the Innovative Medicine segment.

**Competitive intensity.** Oncology and immunology are among the most actively invested therapeutic areas in biopharma. JNJ faces competition from biosimilar manufacturers (Sandoz, Amgen) on legacy products and from innovators (argenx, UCB in immunology; multiple players in CAR-T) on growth franchises. In MedTech, orthopaedics share is under pressure from more focused competitors (Stryker, Zimmer Biomet).

**M&A execution and integration risk.** The strategy depends on serial large acquisitions to fill revenue gaps. Overpayment or integration failure on multi-billion-dollar bets (Intra-Cellular $14.5B, Shockwave $13.1B) is a real risk, acknowledged by structural sources.

**Offsetting factors:** The breadth of the growth portfolio (Darzalex, Tremfya, Carvykti, Rybrevant/Lazcluze, Spravato, plus MedTech cardiovascular platforms) provides multiple independent growth vectors, reducing single-product dependency. The dual-pillar business model creates cross-disciplinary optionality that narrower peers lack. FCF generation ($19.7B) sustains both reinvestment and shareholder returns without balance-sheet strain.

## 4. Qualitative Assessment

**Assessment: Positive on franchise quality; Neutral-to-positive on near-term fundamental attractiveness.**

Johnson & Johnson possesses a durable, wide-moat healthcare franchise with structural growth drivers that are actively offsetting its largest patent cliff. The post-Kenvue portfolio is leaner, higher-margin, and more focused. Execution in recent quarters has been strong — revenue accelerating to +9.9% in Q1 2026, with both segments contributing meaningfully. The oncology and next-generation immunology pipelines provide a credible multi-year growth bridge.

However, the Stelara headwind remains material and is not yet fully absorbed; talc litigation is an unquantified tail risk; and the stock trades at a premium (Morningstar $190 fair value, ~26x earnings per daveahern.substack.com) that prices in much of the good news. The narrative supports a fundamentally sound, defensive franchise with modest growth — consistent with a quality holding — but does not signal an obvious dislocation or underappreciated catalyst at current levels.
